intro.title: About Balcóns de Madrid
intro.description: Welcome to **Balcóns de Madrid**, a panoramic viewpoint over the Sil River Canyon in **Parada de Sil**, **Ourense**, **Galicia**. It is one of the most photographed overlooks of the **Ribeira Sacra** and a favourite stop for travellers exploring the interior of southern Galicia.
intro.descriptionPlain: Welcome to Balcóns de Madrid, a panoramic viewpoint over the Sil River Canyon in Parada de Sil, Ourense, Galicia. It is one of the most photographed overlooks of the Ribeira Sacra.
intro.extendedDescription: Balcóns de Madrid (also known locally as **Os Torgás**) is a free, public viewpoint set on a granite promontory above the Sil. From the railings you look out over a tight meander of the river and the terraced vineyards that define the Ribeira Sacra wine landscape. The short walk from the parking area makes it an easy stop for most visitors.
intro.etymologyTitle: Why is a Galician viewpoint called «Madrid»?
intro.etymologyDescription: According to the **Ribeira Sacra** tourist office, the name does not refer to the Spanish capital directly. Local tradition says that from this promontory the women of Parada de Sil watched their husbands and sons leave for **Madrid** to make a living — many of them as travelling sellers of **barquillos** (wafers). The viewpoint became known as the «balconies of Madrid» because it was the place from which the village saw its people depart towards the capital. The Galician spelling **Balcóns** (with the grave accent on the «ó» and the plural ending) is the correct local form; in Spanish it appears as **Balcones de Madrid**.

sections.title: The name and its local meaning
sections.content: The promontory is known in Galician as **Balcóns de Madrid** and locally as **Os Torgás**. The Ribeira Sacra tourist office explains the name through local memory: from this high point the women of Parada de Sil watched their husbands and sons set off for **Madrid**, many of them working as travelling sellers of **barquillos** (wafers). The overlook became «the balconies of Madrid» — the place the village used to gaze after its people heading to the capital. Keep the spelling in mind when searching: **Balcóns** (Galician) and **Balcones** (Spanish) both refer to the same viewpoint.

sections.title: The Sil Canyon & the Ribeira Sacra
sections.content: Balcóns de Madrid sits on the granite edge of the **Sil River Canyon**, the defining landscape of the **Ribeira Sacra** («Sacred Shore»). Over millions of years the Sil carved a deep gorge — in places several hundred metres vertical — and medieval monastic communities terraced its slopes into the vineyards (socalcos) that today produce the protected Ribeira Sacra wines. The viewpoint captures one of the canyon's tightest meanders, with layered vineyard benches descending to the river.

sections.title: Nature & conservation
sections.content: The surroundings are part of the Natura 2000 network (Site of Community Importance **ES1120005**, «Canyons of the Sil and Cúa rivers»). The canyon is home to birds of prey and native vegetation typical of inland Galicia, including oak, cork oak and the strawberry tree (*Arbutus unedo*). Because it is a sensitive ecosystem, follow Leave No Trace principles: take your rubbish with you, stay on the paths and avoid disturbing wildlife, especially during the breeding season.

hours.title: Visiting Hours & Seasons
hours.bestTimeSpring: Spring (Apr–Jun): blossom, chestnut & almond trees in flower, hiking without heat
hours.bestTimeAutumn: Autumn (Sep–Nov): Vineyards at harvest, oaks in ochre & red tones. Golden Hour 18:30–20:00
hours.bestTimeWinter: Winter (Dec–Mar): Morning mist till 10:30, dreamlike landscapes. Avoid heavy rain days
hours.goldenHourSunrise: Sunrise (20 min before – 20 min after): warm light illuminating the Sil riverbed from the east
hours.goldenHourSunset: Sunset (Golden Hour): optimal time for long-exposure landscape photography of the canyon
hours.blueHourDesc: 20–30 min after sunset (clear days): violet reflections on the Sil water and silhouette of the promontory against the sky
hours.tip: The viewpoint is accessible 24 hours a day. Avoid remaining after dark due to dense fog and disorientation; local roads have no public lighting.

transport.title: How to Get There
transport.fromCenterDesc: By car via OU-201 / OU-204: approximately 72 km (1 h 15 min). The final stretch (OU-204) has tight curves and slopes; caution with large vehicles is recommended.
transport.fromStationDesc: The viewpoint is about 1 km from the village of Parada de Sil. By car, follow the signs from the town hall: the drive takes roughly 4 minutes to the designated parking area, after which it is a flat ~200 m walk along a dirt path to the balconies. On foot from the village square, allow about 15–20 minutes.
transport.fromAirportDesc: Vigo-Peinador Airport (VGO): ~120 km (1 h 40 min). Santiago de Compostela Airport (SCQ): ~145 km (2 h). A rental car is recommended.
transport.publicTransportDesc: There is no regular public transport right to the viewpoint. The Mancomunidade da Ribeira Sacra Interior runs an on-demand transport service (book at least 48 h ahead); check availability at the Town Council of Parada de Sil.
transport.walkingDesc: From the designated parking area, a short dirt trail of about 200 m leads to the balconies. From the village square of Parada de Sil it is roughly a 1 km walk (about 15–20 minutes, gentle).
transport.drivingDesc: A private car is the most practical option. The last kilometre is a single-lane unpaved track with passing places. Larger vehicles (tour buses) should check access with the Concello in high season.

route.title: Visit Routes by Difficulty Level
route.intro: Three short circuits are suggested according to available time and interest. All routes start and end at the Balcóns de Madrid parking area.

levels.audience: Suitable for: occasional hikers, closed sports footwear, 500 ml water/person
levels.highlights: Content: both balconies, tour through terraced vineyard benches, bird-of-prey observation point, return via a signposted trail. Protected cultural landscape DO Ribeira Sacra.

Descent along the trail to the bird observation point
Stretch along vineyard terraces, respecting private property
Connection with the forest track and return along the eastern slope

hotels.title: Types of Accommodation in the Area (Typological Information)
hotels.subtitle: Neutral information by lodging category · No specific establishments are recommended
hotels.disclaimer: The following describes, for exclusively informative purposes and without commercial recommendation, the different typologies of accommodation in the comarca. Travellers are invited to consult the official public platforms of the Xunta de Galicia and the Register of Tourist Accommodation of Galicia.

categories.name: Rural Tourism (Casa Rural / Aldea Rural)
categories.suitableFor: Profile: families, couples, groups seeking tranquility and direct personal treatment
categories.features: Features: rehabilitated traditional Galician building (stone + slate roof), self-catering or half board, fireplace, hórreo (granary). Typical distance to viewpoint: 4 to 18 km along local roads.
categories.average: Common range: 2 – 4 bedrooms · minimum stay 1-2 nights

categories.name: Agrotourism & Farmhouse Stays
categories.suitableFor: Profile: travellers interested in local gastronomy, contact with agricultural life, children
categories.features: Features: accommodation integrated into active holdings (vineyard, chestnut grove, organic vegetable garden). Possibility to join grape harvest, bread or cheese making. Average distance to viewpoint: 6 to 22 km.
categories.average: Common range: 2-5 bedrooms · full board frequent

categories.name: Youth & Pilgrim Hostels
categories.suitableFor: Profile: backpackers, walkers, students, individual travellers on a tight budget
categories.features: Features: dormitories, shared bathrooms, community kitchen. Municipal and parish hostels operate in the Ribeira Sacra, as well as private hostels. Nearest to the viewpoint: Monforte de Lemos (≈ 28 km).
categories.average: Common range: 10 – 50 beds · high season April-October

categories.name: Camping / Motorhome Areas
categories.suitableFor: Profile: motorhome owners, families with tents, outdoor enthusiasts
categories.features: Features: delimited pitches, sanitary services, grey and black water discharge, electricity and water. Nearest campsite is some distance away; consult municipal ordinances for motorhome areas in the comarca.
categories.average: Note: overnight stay in motorhomes at the viewpoint car park is not permitted (Concello de Parada de Sil ordinance).

categories.name: Town Hotels & Hostals
categories.suitableFor: Profile: guests preferring standard services, breakfast included, 24 h reception
categories.features: Features: in population centres (Monforte de Lemos, Ourense, Quiroga). Category from 1 to 4 stars. Typical distances to viewpoint: 22 to 72 km; daily travel by private vehicle or taxi.
categories.average: Common range: from single room to family suites

amenities.title: Services & Facilities Around the Area
amenities.subtitle: Neutral typological information · No specific commercial establishments are mentioned
amenities.disclaimer: The following lists the typology of services within a radius of a few to several dozen km of the viewpoint. For specific locations, consult the official directories of the Concello de Parada de Sil and Turismo Galicia.

categories.name: Toilets & Hygiene Services
categories.summary: There are **no permanent public toilets** at the viewpoint itself. Use the services in Parada de Sil before going. In high season the Concello may place a portable chemical toilet module in the parking area. Follow Leave No Trace: do not deposit waste or toilet paper in nature.
categories.distance: Nearest fixed toilets: in Parada de Sil (about 1 km)

categories.name: Parking
categories.summary: A small unpaved parking area with limited spaces, free of charge. On sunny weekends of July, August and Holy Week it usually fills before late morning; a waiting area may be activated nearby. Park only in the designated area — not on the shoulders of the access track.

categories.name: Gastronomic Offer Types (Typologies)
categories.summary: Categories of gastronomic establishments within a radius of 6 to 30 km, without naming specific businesses: (a) Galician pulperías (octopus restaurants) and cider houses; (b) traditional dining houses and mesón (set daily menu); (c) signature cuisine with a DO Ribeira Sacra wine list; (d) café-bar with pastries (nearby villages); (e) traditional bakery. Lunch hours in Galicia are generally 1:30–4:00 p.m.
categories.distance: Nearest nucleus with meal offer: ≈ 6 km

categories.name: Supermarkets, Groceries & Bakery
categories.summary: The viewpoint has no retail outlets. Stock up in a centre with supermarket and basic pantry before going. Existing typologies: conventional supermarkets, cooperative supermarkets, artisan bakeries, butcher shops, fishmongers, greengrocers. Take water (min. 0.5 L/person), nuts and fruit.

categories.name: Petrol Stations & Electric Vehicle Charging
categories.summary: Conventional service stations exist in the main centres of the comarca. Public EV charging in the interior of the Ribeira Sacra is limited, so leave with the battery charged. The nearest fast charger is in Monforte de Lemos. Refuel before entering secondary roads.
categories.distance: Nearest petrol station: ≈ 12 km · Fast EV charger: Monforte de Lemos

categories.name: Accessibility & Reduced Mobility
categories.summary: Asphalted road to the car park. From car park to the Main Balcony: ~180 m section with moderate slope — accessible with assisted wheelchair, not autonomous. Secondary Balcony: not accessible (steps and dirt path). No permanent adapted toilets. Assistance dogs admitted without restriction.
categories.distance: Check annual improvements on the Concello de Parada de Sil website

categories.name: Companion Animals & Pets
categories.summary: Dogs must be **leashed at all times** per the municipal ordinance and Natura 2000 rules (to avoid disturbing birds of prey and wildlife). Carry and pick up droppings bags. Avoid bringing pets during the bird breeding season (March – July). No public drinking trough at the viewpoint; bring extra water for dogs in summer.
categories.distance: Notice: do not deposit droppings in the forest

categories.name: Healthcare & Emergencies
categories.summary: General emergency telephone 112 (Spain). The nearest medical practice operates in the morning at the Parada de Sil health centre. Reference hospital: Hospital de Ourense (≈ 72 km). If you suffer from vertigo, do not approach the edge; in summer bring SPF ≥ 30, hat and water; tick incidence on trails is moderate.
categories.distance: Nearest health centre: Parada de Sil (about 1 km) · County hospital: ≈ 72 km

items.question: Where is Balcóns de Madrid located?
items.answer: Balcóns de Madrid is in Parada de Sil, Ourense, Galicia, Spain — about 1 km from the village, above the Sil River Canyon in the Ribeira Sacra.

items.question: Is Balcóns de Madrid free to visit?
items.answer: Yes. Balcóns de Madrid is a free, public viewpoint, open all year round.

items.question: How do you get to Balcóns de Madrid?
items.answer: From the village of Parada de Sil, follow the signs from the town hall: about a 4-minute drive to the designated parking area, then a flat ~200 m walk along a dirt path to the balconies. On foot from the village square it is roughly 1 km (15–20 minutes).

items.question: Is it Balcóns, Balcones or Balcón de Madrid?
items.answer: All refer to the same viewpoint. The local Galician spelling is **Balcóns de Madrid** (grave accent on the «ó», plural); in Spanish it appears as **Balcones de Madrid**. It is also known locally as **Os Torgás** and as the **Mirador de los Balcones de Madrid**.

items.question: Why is it called Balcóns de Madrid if it is in Galicia?
items.answer: According to the Ribeira Sacra tourist office, local women of Parada de Sil watched from here as their husbands and sons left for Madrid — many working as travelling sellers of wafers (barquillos). The overlook became «the balconies of Madrid». The Galician **Balcóns** and the Spanish **Balcones** are the same place.

items.question: What facilities are there at the viewpoint?
items.answer: There are no permanent toilets or public fountains at the viewpoint. A small free parking area is nearby. In high season the Concello may place a portable toilet module. Bring water and use the services in Parada de Sil (about 1 km).
